purpose: Path shapes crafted to slip past a naive comparison. Every one must be refused, and none may be silently normalised into an admitted path.

expected.why: Traversal must be refused rather than resolved, because resolving it would land in a sibling grant.
A '.' segment is not a path git would report and hides the real target.
An absolute path escapes the repository entirely.
A doubled separator produces an empty segment that some matchers skip.
Backslash separators would be one opaque segment, and treating them as separators would widen the grant.
A drive-letter path is not repository-relative.
A trailing separator names a directory; git reports files.
A git-quoted path means the caller forgot -z; the quotes would defeat every glob.
A NUL byte truncates the path in any C-level consumer.
A newline splits the path in line-oriented tooling.
Git pathspecs are case-sensitive, so a case variant is a different path and is not granted.
A suffixed sibling directory must not inherit the grant.
A literal '*' in a changed path must be matched as a character, never expanded as a wildcard.
A zero-width space makes the segment visually identical to the granted one.
A nested repository inside the owned subtree is still repository internals.
